To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) adult cold tolerance is enhanced in the spring, (2) adult heat tolerance is not enhanced in the spring or in the summer, (3) geographic variation in cold and heat tolerance is not due to direct selection on adults, and (4) geographic variation in adult cold tolerance is due to geographic variation in the acclimation response to spring-like temperatures.
the evolution of thermal tolerance in seasonal environments is shaped by the interaction between life-history timing and annual temperature profiles.

(i) adult cold tolerance is enhanced by thermal acclimation, (ii) adult cold tolerance varies with geographic origin, and (iii) geographic variation in cold stress exposure is consistent with the timing of adult activity.

understanding the evolutionary consequences of seasonal variation in temperature.

the evolution and consequences of thermal adaptation in organisms with complex life histories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there are significant geographic differences in the acclimation responses of adult mosquitoes to temperature, but the differences are not due to differences in the timing of diapause, but rather due to differences in temperature profiles.
the evolution of thermotolerance in seasonal environments is dependent on life-history timing.
the evolution of thermal tolerance depends on the life history and the seasonal temperature profile of the species in question.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adaptive value of cold tolerance is determined by the timing of adult activity in the seasonal environment.
the evolution of thermal acclimation and life-history timing are intimately linked and that the evolution of one can be constrained by the other.
the evolution of cold tolerance in seasonal environments depends on the timing of life-history stages, the thermal environment, and the thermal sensitivity of life-history stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adaptive value of thermal tolerance depends strongly on the seasonal environment and on the life-history timing of an organism.
seasonal temperature variation can be as important as mean temperature in driving the evolution of thermal tolerance in organisms with complex life histories.

the adaptive value of thermal traits in seasonal environments depends on the life stage that experiences the stress, the seasonal timing of the stress, and the degree to which thermal traits are acclimated.
